claim: History, not a forecast. A savings bond held 20 years is guaranteed to reach at least double its price (about 3.53% a year). Rolling 3-month T-bills for 20 years, starting any month from 1934 to 2006 (873 starts), ended above double in 52.3% of starts (median multiple 2.097; range 1.129 to 4.612). It was a matter of era: starts from the 1950s through the 1980s mostly beat double, while starts from 1990 on beat it in only 5.0% of months, and the latest full stretch (Sep 2006 to Aug 2026) turned money into 1.378 times. Double itself is not inflation-proof: it kept up with consumer prices over 20 years in 58.7% of start months (median buying power 107.3% of the original). In Aug 2026 the 3-month bill rate was 3.72%.

numbers.definition: Number of 20-year start months. T-bill roll: money invested at the start of month s earns TB3MS/12 percent in each of the 240 months s, s+1, ..., s+239 (simple monthly roll at the quoted rate, compounded monthly): multiple M(s) = product over those months of (1 + TB3MS/1200). Start months: every TB3MS month with 240 months of data from s onward, i.e. 1934-01-01 .. 2006-09-01. The savings bond's value at 20 years is taken as exactly 2.0 x purchase price. TB3MS = 3-month Treasury bill secondary market rate, discount basis, percent, monthly average, pinned FRED CSV (coed=2026-08-01, first observation 1934-01-01). CPIAUCNS = CPI-U all items, US city average, not seasonally adjusted, pinned FRED CSV (coed=2026-08-01; 2025-10-01 is blank).

100 x (real-window start months with 2.0 x CPIAUCNS(s)/CPIAUCNS(s+240) >= 1) / real_windows, rounded to 0.1: how often a doubled amount bought at least as much as the original amount 20 years earlier.

assumptions: The doubling guarantee is applied to every historical start as if it had existed then (it applies to bonds issued from May 2005; before that, bonds had other terms). The comparison is hypothetical for earlier starts.

T-bill returns use the monthly average 3-month rate divided by 12 each month (discount-basis rate, not converted to investment yield), compounded monthly; transaction costs and gaps between rolls are ignored.
Taxes are ignored: T-bill interest is federally taxed each year, while savings bond interest is federally tax-deferred until redemption; both are exempt from state income tax.
Savings bonds cashed before 20 years earn only their stated fixed rate (and lose 3 months of interest before 5 years); the comparison assumes a full 20-year hold.
Annual purchase limits on savings bonds are ignored.

provisions.cite: 31 CFR 351.34(a) (Series EE bonds issued May 1, 2005 or later: original maturity)
provisions.quote: Bonds reach original maturity at 20 years after the issue date

provisions.cite: 31 CFR 351.35(f)(2) (redemption value of book-entry Series EE bonds at original maturity)
provisions.quote: At original maturity, the redemption value of a book-entry bond shall not be less than double the purchase price of the bond.
